narrative_purpose: Show the two machines behind a magnetic sense — the light-driven radical-pair compass inside the eye that reads field direction, and the magnetite crystals that read field intensity as a map — so the reader grasps how an animal can feel a field we cannot.
subject: A two-part naturalist diagram. On one side, a cutaway of an eye with a single glowing protein molecule splitting into a linked pair of glowing points (a radical pair), faint magnetic field contour lines overlaid across the retina like a compass. On the other side, a chain of small dark angular crystals inside a cell, physically tugging on a fine nerve fibre.
scene: A dark study ground, the two mechanisms set apart in their own pools of glow against deep indigo.
camera: Flat diagrammatic study view, close on each mechanism.
light: Cool bioluminescent glow from the radical pair and the field lines; the magnetite chain catching a hard cool rim; deep shadow surround.
palette: Void-indigo ground, Pandora cyan and living teal for the molecular glow and field lines, magenta accent on the active radical pair.
style: Painterly speculative-biology diagram plate, hand-painted, clean and observed.
detail_level: Crisp on the molecule, the field-line overlay and the crystal chain; plain dark background.
composition: Two clear zones side by side — eye-compass left, magnetite-map right — each ringed with dark open space for labels.
consistency_notes: Cool Pandora palette and from-within glow; field lines should read as a perceived overlay, not a technical schematic.
negative_prompt: no text, no lettering, no numbers, no logos, no diagram labels, no arrows, no equations, no photographic or 3D-render look, no lens flares, no neon UI glow, no cartoon or anime style
